text:
nina: heads-up — support ticket says they were billed twice when a stream truncated & client retried. ui shows overlapping provisional + confirmed rows.

carlos: can you paste request/session ids and the region?

nina: req=rq-204 / sess=ss-7f2 in eu-west. client observed early EOF, retried, server resumed and replayed last 70 tokens.

tess: logs for ss-7f2: 
```
2026-03-12T18:40:10Z ingress: new-session sess=ss-7f2 provisional_tokens=240
2026-03-12T18:40:15Z runtime: stream-truncate reason=client_eof emitted_prefix=70
2026-03-12T18:40:18Z router: start-resume sess=ss-7f2 target=pool-b
2026-03-12T18:40:19Z ledger: provisional_insert sess=ss-7f2 tokens=70
2026-03-12T18:40:21Z ledger: confirm_charge sess=ss-7f2 tokens=70
```

tess: looks like resume wrote a new provisional and then a confirm, while the original provisional (from initial stream) wasn't tombstoned. double-count.

own: noticed last week we had a similar race but for leader re-election. Root cause seems to be no stable prefix identifier across handoffs. router just treats the resumed prefix as a fresh provisional.

nina: UX problem: customers interpret two rows as two charges. We need both a short-term console mitigation and a long-term ledger fix.

carlos: long-term approach idea: generate a prefix_id at first emission (prefix_id = sha1(req_id + prefix_start)). Carry prefix_id through handoffs. Ledger provisional rows include prefix_id. Confirm operation upserts by prefix_id instead of inserting an independent confirm row.

own: yep. upsert semantics remove the double-row. Also track a provenance field on the finalized charge so we can show "merged from provisional" in the UI.

tess: short-term console mitigation: collapse rows where sess matches and token ranges overlap >50% within a 24h window, mark as "suspected-merge" and hide the provisional by default. Provide an "expand" to see raw rows for auditors.

nina: telemetry: we'll add these metrics 
- billing.prov_upsert_attempts (counter)
- billing.duplicate_confirm_alerts (counter)
- billing.prov_confirm_lag_ms (histogram)
so we can detect if upserts are happening frequently.

carlos: infra plan:
1) router: attach prefix_id to token-emission span and propagate via handoff RPC (feature-flagged).
2) ledger: implement upsert by prefix_id; fallback to old flow if prefix_id absent. Add DB index on prefix_id with TTL of 72h.
3) reconciliation: accept upsert events; for now emit both an audit insert and a merged-event so older consumers aren't broken.
4) console: read-side detect prefix_id and merge rows; show merged badge with link to audit rows.

own: tests: unit for ledger.upsert, integration simulating concurrent handoff where original provisional tombstone races with resume confirm. Add chaos test to simulate packet loss and ensure no double billing.

tess: rollout: keep flags off by default. Enable prefix_id propagation in router in canary region, enable ledger upsert behind flag, then enable console merge. Monitor billing.duplicate_confirm_alerts.

billing-bot: created ticket BILL-2026-128 and alert billing.duplicate_confirms > 3/min for any tenant.

nina: i'll draft the PR for router today and include a small protocol doc on prefix_id lifetime and collision policy (short lived, random salt per router instance).

carlos: nice. also consider adding a debug view in console for prov_id traces to help customer support.

own: one more thought — for long requests with multiple truncation/resume cycles, ensure prefix_id is per prefix range (start offset) not global session so confirms map to the right prefix.

tess: good call. keep prefix granularity = (req_id, prefix_start, prefix_len) hashed to prefix_id.

nina: thanks all. post-PR we'll run a quick reconciliation job for the last 48h to merge obvious dupes and annotate billing notes for affected customers.

carlos: assign me ledger work. nina takes router; tess takes tests; owen adds recon changes.

nina: dropped the session ids here for traceability. please post any other examples.

carlos: +1 will follow up in PR review.
